CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION — NARRATIVE INPATIENT DISCHARGE SUMMARY V1
Patient: Patricia Williams | MRN: PAT-60004 | DOB: 1980-02-19 | Gender: Female | Doc ID: NARRATIVE_0004
Encounter Date: 2025-02-25 | Discharge/Note Date: 2025-02-27 | Provider: Dr. Marcus Vance, DO
CHIEF COMPLAINT
The patient presented with epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, and poor oral intake.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 78-year-old female with a medical history pertinent for hypertension and dyslipidemia who presented for
evaluation of epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, and poor oral intake. Symptoms began approximately four days prior to
admission and escalated in severity. On presentation to the emergency department, initial diagnostic evaluation
demonstrated that sodium was 140.2 mmol/L. Concurrently, serum chemistry was notable for a glucose of 87.8 mg/dL. Vital
signs upon arrival were stable, and the patient was admitted to the inpatient general medicine service.
HOSPITAL COURSE
During the hospital course, the inpatient team initiated targeted management. The patient received Amlodipine 2.5 mg by
mouth once daily with good clinical tolerance. Serial assessments revealed gradual resolution of presenting symptoms. Prior
to planned discharge, repeat laboratory testing confirmed that bun stabilized at 13.7 mg/dL. The patient was ambulating
without assistance and tolerating a regular diet.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS
The patient was discharged home in stable clinical condition with instructions to take Lisinopril 40 mg PO every morning,
and Atorvastatin 10 mg orally once daily at bedtime. Medication reconciliation was completed and all questions regarding
dosing schedules were answered.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS & FOLLOW-UP
The patient was advised to follow up with their primary care physician within 7 to 10 days. Return precautions for chest pain,
recurrent shortness of breath, or fever were provided and understood.
